record.name: Libya
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. A National AI Strategy 2026-2030 and an AI Ethics Charter were launched in June 2026, with a proposed ethics oversight body but no technical safety or evaluation institute.

English searches for a national AI safety, security or evaluation institute, commitment, proposal or study. No qualifying institute or commitment was identified in the English search. The retained ESCWA primary article describes work with the General Information Authority on a national AI strategy draft and public-sector implementation. check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: ESCWA describes its own workshop with Libya's General Information Authority. SMEX publishes a separately authored critical reading of the later strategy and ethics charter, including their oversight body's design and executive dependence. SMEX's substantive analysis is not a republication of ESCWA's workshop account. These are two independent contextual origins, not explicit official denials.
check.governance_note: The General Information Authority reports adoption of the ethics charter and launch of the AI strategy; UN ESCWA describes the strategy-development process.

related_bodies.name: General Information Authority
related_bodies.role: It led the drafting of the AI Ethics Charter and, with ESCWA, the strategy.

related_bodies.name: National oversight body for AI ethics (proposed)
related_bodies.role: It is proposed in the charter under the Council of Ministers to supervise compliance and approve high-risk systems; pre-deployment assessment stays with the deploying institution. This was reported by SMEX.

record.notes: Libya's General Information Authority reported adoption of the national AI ethics charter and launch of the 2026-2030 AI strategy in June 2026. The proposed ethics oversight body and post-deployment audit design remain described by SMEX; the underlying charter was not fully read. No qualifying evaluation institute was found in this bounded review. SMEX attributes the launch to the Government of National Unity at a ceremony in Tripoli and reports that the strategy's risk register flags political instability and institutional fragmentation. This is not evidence of adoption by every Libyan authority. OECD.AI gives 2025-2030, whereas the General Information Authority and SMEX use 2026-2030; the discrepancy was not resolved from the full strategy text.

next_check.reason: Whether the proposed AI ethics oversight body is created and given a testing mandate.

sources.title: National artificial intelligence strategy in Libya

excerpts.text: On 14 October, ESCWA organized a hybrid workshop in collaboration with the General Information Authority (GIA) in Libya to support the development of the country’s national AI strategy.

sources.title: Libya's new AI strategy celebrates participation, yet was built without it

excerpts.text: The charter proposes a “national oversight body for AI ethics” to supervise compliance, approve high-risk systems, and maintain a registry of “ethical compliance” certifications.
